description:
## Goal Fill in `guides/Migration Guide.md` with a phased guide for converting an existing Phoenix LiveView (assigns-based) application to use Filament. The file already exists as an empty stub — fill it in. Do NOT create a new file. The guide covers: identifying what's in assigns, extracting domain state into a GenServer, replacing handle_event with event closures, adding projections, and a note on codemods where the transformation is automatable. ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## 0. Prerequisites — read guides first Before writing this guide, read the completed guides from I2, I3, and I4: - `guides/Getting Started.md` - `guides/Observables.md` - `guides/Resource Holds.md` The migration guide assumes the reader has read "Getting Started" and references those guides for background. --- ## 1. File to fill in FILE: `guides/Migration Guide.md` --- ## 2. Guide outline ### Overview (≤ 150 words) Who this guide is for: developers with an existing Phoenix LiveView app who want to adopt Filament incrementally. Filament is not all-or-nothing — you can add it to one LiveView at a time using `Filament.LiveComponent`. Reference the I5 interop adapter: a single `<.live_component>` tag is the entry point. ### Phase 1: Add Filament to your project Show the `mix.exs` change: ```elixir {:filament, "~> 0.1"} ``` No other changes needed. Filament does not require Phoenix or LiveView to be replaced. ### Phase 2: Identify your assigns Show a representative before-state — a simple LiveView with assigns-based state: ```elixir defmodule MyApp.CartLive do use Phoenix.LiveView def mount(_params, _session, socket) do {:ok, assign(socket, items: [], total: 0)} end def handle_event("add_item", %{"id" => id, "name" => name, "price" => price}, socket) do item = %{id: id, name: name, price: String.to_integer(price)} items = socket.assigns.items ++ [item] total = Enum.sum(Enum.map(items, & &1.price)) {:noreply, assign(socket, items: items, total: total)} end end ``` Classify assigns by type: - **Ephemeral UI state** (filter selection, form input) → `use_state` in component - **Shared domain state** (cart contents, user profile) → `Observable.GenServer` - **Resource claims** (checkout lock, seat hold) → `Hold.GenServer` - **Derived/computed** (total_cents from items) → either `use_memo` or computed in server state ### Phase 3: Extract domain state into Observable.GenServer Walk through converting `items` and `total` from LiveView assigns to a GenServer: ```elixir defmodule MyApp.CartServer do use Filament.Observable.GenServer def start_link(opts \\ []) do GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, %{items: [], total: 0}, name: Keyword.get(opts, :name, __MODULE__)) end @impl Filament.Observable def handle_subscribe(_req, _sub, state), do: {:ok, state, state} @impl GenServer def handle_call({:add_item, item}, _from, state) do items = state.items ++ [item] total = Enum.sum(Enum.map(items, & &1.price)) new_state = %{state | items: items, total: total} notify_observers(new_state) {:reply, :ok, new_state} end end ``` Point to the Observables guide for the full Observable.GenServer explanation. ### Phase 4: Convert the LiveView to a Filament component Show the after-state using `use Filament.Component` and `use_observable`: ```elixir defmodule MyApp.CartComponent do use Filament.Component defcomponent MyApp.CartComponent do prop :server, :any, default: MyApp.CartServer def render(assigns) do cart = use_observable(@server) ~F\"""
    <%= for item <- (cart || %{items: []}).items do %>
  • {item.name} — {item.price}
    • <% end %>

Total: {(cart || %{total: 0}).total}

\""" end end end ``` NOTE: Use actual ~F template syntax from the examples — not `<%= %>` if Filament uses `{}` interpolation. Adapt the code to match what the ~F sigil actually supports. ### Phase 5: Embed in the existing LiveView (incremental adoption) Show how to use `Filament.LiveComponent` to embed the new component in the existing LiveView without replacing the whole LiveView: ```heex <%# In existing LiveView template: %> <.live_component module={Filament.LiveComponent} id="cart" component={MyApp.CartComponent} /> ``` And the handle_info forwarding pattern (required for observable updates): ```elixir def handle_info({type, _fid, _slot, _val} = msg, socket) when type in [:filament_set_state, :filament_observable_update, :filament_observable_resubscribe] do Phoenix.LiveView.send_update(Filament.LiveComponent, id: "cart", filament_msg: msg) {:noreply, socket} end ``` Reference the Observables guide for the full observable pattern. ### Phase 6: Full migration (optional) Once all components are Filament components, replace `use Phoenix.LiveView` with `use Filament.LiveView`: ```elixir defmodule MyApp.CartLive do use Filament.LiveView def root_component, do: MyApp.CartComponent end ``` This removes the need for the handle_info forwarding pattern. ### Codemods (where automatable) Note which transformations are mechanical enough for a codemod: - `assign(socket, key: value)` → `use_state(key, value)` (for local UI state) - `socket.assigns.key` → `@key` in ~F templates - `handle_event("event", params, socket) → event closure These are not shipped as actual codemod tools in this release. This section is a pointer for teams who want to automate the transformation. A community codemod PR would be welcome. --- ## 3. Style guidelines (same as I2–I4) - Present tense, second person. - Code blocks are valid Elixir. Adapt ALL example code to match actual Filament API (read the source before writing — do not invent syntax). - ≤ 200 words per section. --- ## 4. Acceptance criteria - [ ] `guides/Migration Guide.md` is non-empty (≥ 400 words) - [ ] All code blocks are valid Elixir - [ ] `mix docs` exits 0 and "Migration Guide" appears in generated site - [ ] Guide covers: incremental adoption via Filament.LiveComponent, Observable.GenServer extraction, full migration via Filament.LiveView, codemods note - [ ] References the Getting Started, Observables, and Resource Holds guides by name - [ ] No references to APIs that don't exist (verify against actual implementations)
